summary: Accenture is multinational management consulting, technology services and outsourcing company, founded in 2001. Type: listed company. About 779,000 employees (Wikidata). Revenue $69.7 billion (2024). Recognised visa sponsor (IND). 88% of its 17 jobs here don't ask for Dutch. News, last 3 months: 2 about funding; 10 about acquisitions; 5 about growth or hiring; 1 about legal trouble, strikes or bankruptcy.

insights.one_liner: Global consulting and tech services firm (779,000 staff in 2025) with 77 open roles here, mostly Amsterdam consulting jobs, and 82% don't require Dutch.

culture.text: Half of its 77 open roles here are in consulting and strategy (38), followed by IT, cloud and security (15); 43 are based in Amsterdam.
A huge company: about 779,000 employees worldwide in 2025, with staff mostly from computer science, IT, engineering and business backgrounds.
Offers summer internships and apprenticeships, and talks about a well-being programme it calls 'Net Better Off'.
Openings lean senior: 28 manager and 17 senior roles versus 8 internships and 4 entry-level jobs.

open.text: Accenture B.V. is an IND recognised visa sponsor.
82% of its 77 jobs here don't require Dutch, and several are shared between Amsterdam and Madrid, London, Berlin or other European cities.
None of its current postings here mention visa or relocation support.

growth.text: Grew from 721,000 to 779,000 employees worldwide between 2022 and 2025.
Made US$69.7 billion revenue and US$7.7 billion net profit in 2024.
Reported double-digit profit growth for fiscal year 2026.
Completed the acquisition of Danish software firm Mjølner Informatics.

worth_knowing.text: Appointed Sjoerd van Gendt as its new Country Managing Director for the Netherlands.
An Accenture contractor was removed from FBI work after a damaging data breach linked to a missed security patch.
Reached a US$25 million settlement in a US False Claims Act case about DEI.
